decisions.reason: It was publicly launched with strong language as a new flagship feature in the firm’s secure identity offering, so management is likely to justify the investment and give it more time to gain adoption.

An identity-bound payment wallet fits the firm’s security and digital identity direction, and with no clear failure evidence yet a mature German software firm would likely continue rather than reverse course after a recent launch.

Although a NFC-based authenticator may be narrower and risk slower uptake, it is still recent enough that management can attribute weak traction to customer adoption and integration delays rather than abandon it quickly.
Having its own product page signals a visible commitment and a strategic role in the firm’s security platform story, which under escalation of commitment makes withdrawal within a year unlikely.
A secure platform for multi-service mobile apps appears central to the firm’s broader strategic positioning, so management would tend to persist and defend the prior investment.
A dedicated page and the product’s close fit with the firm’s core security capabilities suggest high sunk commitment, making continued support much more likely than an early exit.
